syntax.guarded_form: @p or.b32 d, a, b;  (or @!p or.b32 d, a, b;)
notes: Destination d, then sources a, b. Predicate guard is external to instruction-description syntax.

b.immediate_note: An example includes a register value and immediate hex literal for .b32, but there is no general per-position immediate grammar in the collected section for or; immediate support is not normalized into the bounded source-form claim.

types.typing_rule: Operands are interpreted in 32-bit width context for the bounded form; size-match rule from or section applies (same-size operands), exact typed-compatibility policy beyond size matching is not made normative at this stage.

guard_semantics.at_p: execute iff predicate p evaluates true
guard_semantics.at_bang_p: execute iff predicate p evaluates false
guard_semantics.false_guard: no state transition in bounded model

state_reads.description: Read source a (register value) and source b when b is a register; read b immediate literal only if parser/domain admits immediate in source position b.
Read predicate operand p when guard present (or its negation) to evaluate complete guard expression.

state_writes.description:
On true guard branch, write d := a OR b, bitwise OR over 32-bit values.
If b is immediate, constant is converted to 32-bit value in the read path before OR.
On false guard branch, bounded model has no state mutation.

design_dependencies.statement: Bounded state is register-and-predicate local state only (value register file plus predicate register file), no explicit memory/special/global control-side channels are modeled for this unit.

State transition is partial in this bounded model only on unresolved operand typing/decoding cases; such non-representable cases map to undefined outcome in this artifact rather than a source-asserted runtime trap.
Single register-write locality: only destination register d is written on the execute branch; no other register components are updated by this bounded rule.

Is bit-bucket destination '_' admissible for or.b32 specifically?

human_assumptions.statement: No cross-instruction or system-level side effects are introduced in this bounded transition beyond value/predicate local state in the architecture model.

semantic_claims.statement: or section defines `or.type d, a, b;` with `.type = { .pred, .b16, .b32, .b64 }`.
Bounded base form is `or.b32 d, a, b;`, i.e., width 32 specialization of the family syntax.
Optional predicate controls execution and `@!p` is negated-prefix form per PTX predication context.
When guard is false, bounded transition is no-op (state unchanged).
Execution writes destination register d with a 32-bit bitwise OR of resolved source values on guard-true branch.
Immediate support for source operand b is supported by an example only and is not yet proven as a general grammar rule for or.b32.
Transition is modeled as partial for unresolved typing/decoding cases; unresolved cases are represented as undefined transition in this bounded artifact.
No explicit exception/error/UB/implementation-defined clause is recorded for or.b32 from the collected source range.
